question.problem:
Let $f(x,y)$ be a differentiable function such that

$$
f(0,3)=8,\,{f}_{x}(x,y)=\frac{4{e}^{2x}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2x}+y}},\,{f}_{y}(x,y)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{{e}^{2x}+y}}.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(0,3),$ estimate the value of $f(-0.05,2.9).$
question.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y)≈f(a,b)+∇f(a,b)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(0,3)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ≈f(0,3)+∇f(0,3)\cdot ⟨x-0,y-3⟩ \\  & =f(0,3)+⟨{f}_{x}(0,3),{f}_{y}(0,3)⟩\cdot ⟨x,y-3⟩ \\  & =8+⟨{f}_{x}(0,3),{f}_{y}(0,3)⟩\cdot ⟨x,y-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{x}(0,3)$ and ${f}_{y}(0,3)$ using the given partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(0,3) & =\frac{4{e}^{2(0)}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2(0)}+3}}=2 \\ {f}_{y}(0,3) & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{{e}^{2(0)}+3}}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y)≈8+⟨2,1⟩\cdot ⟨x,y-3⟩.
$$

Finally, we can estimate $f(-0.05,2.9)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=-0.05$ and $y=2.9,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-0.05,2.9) & ≈8+⟨2,1⟩\cdot ⟨-0.05,2.9-3⟩ \\  & =8+⟨2,1⟩\cdot ⟨-0.05,-0.1⟩ \\  & =8-0.1-0.1 \\  & =7.8\end{aligned}
$$
